title: Ribeye with Garlic and Mint Butter
summary: A thin ribeye seared hard and fast in a stainless-steel pan, then basted with garlic and fresh mint butter. About three minutes in the pan.

steps.text: Season the steak with salt and black pepper and leave it out for {timer:15-20}. Pat it dry just before cooking if the surface has become wet.
Put the empty stainless-steel pan over a medium-high heat for {timer:2-3}.
Test it with a tiny drop of water: when it forms a little ball that skates around the pan rather than evaporating at once, the pan is ready.
Add the oil and swirl it around. Give it {timer:10-15s}.
Lay the steak in the pan, away from you. It should sizzle straight away. Cook the first side for {timer:90s} without moving it; once a crust forms it will release on its own.
Turn it and cook the second side for {timer:1}.
Turn the heat down to medium-low and add the butter and the garlic.
When the butter foams, add the mint leaves and baste the steak continuously for {timer:30s}, tilting the pan and spooning the butter over.
Take the steak out when the centre reaches {temp:52-53!} for medium-rare.
Rest it uncovered on a warm plate for {timer:4-5}, and spoon a little of the garlic and mint butter over it before serving.

tips: Do not start with the butter: at searing heat it burns. Sear in oil, then add the butter, garlic and mint once the heat is down.
Mint burns quickly, which is why it goes in only for the last moments: it stays aromatic rather than bitter.
A thin steak needs about 3 minutes in the pan in all. Trust the thermometer over the timings: if it reaches 52 °C early, take it out at once. It settles at 54-56 °C after resting.
These timings are for a steak about 1.5-2 cm thick.
